title: Reading Drill — Reducing repeated journeys to a tool shed — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Reducing repeated journeys to a tool shed — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Hillswick, work on gardeners discovering that the right tools are already borrowed had already produced a small collection of checkout records. The allotment committee used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: extra trips per afternoon.

**B** The group kept a board listing tools in use for the new trial, which was planned to run for five weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that occasional large classes should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
